Use this sheet with `exercise-student.html` if RStudio is unavailable. Predict
before reading a table, then interpret in words. Results are exact Beta
calculations or the supplied default Stan fit; no new inference was run.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(posterior)
library(here)
source(here("R/course_utils.R"))
theme_set(theme_bw())
fit <- fit_or_load("day1_seedling", "stan/binomial.stan",
                  list(N=5,y=2,a=1,b=1), use_precomputed=TRUE)
draws <- fit$draws
```

## 1A: prior and data comparisons

```{r comparisons}
cases <- tribble(~y,~N,~a,~b, 2,5,1,1, 8,20,1,1, 40,100,1,1,
                 2,5,2,2, 2,5,8,2, 40,100,8,2)
knitr::kable(pmap_dfr(cases, summarise_update),digits=3)
plot_update(2,5,8,2)
```

The first three rows keep the observed proportion and prior fixed. A strong
prior changes the small-data posterior more than the large-data posterior.
For 2/5 and the flat prior, $P(p>0.5\mid y)=`r round(1-pbeta(.5,3,4),3)`$.

## 1B: draws, probability statements and prediction

```{r draws-summary}
knitr::kable(summarise_draws(subset_draws(draws,variable="p"),mean,
                           ~quantile(.x,c(.05,.95)),rhat,ess_bulk,ess_tail),digits=3)
knitr::kable(diagnostic_table(fit))
```

There are `r nrow(draws)` retained draws (4 chains × 1000).
$P(p>0.5\mid y)$ from these draws is `r round(mean(draws$p>.5),3)`.
Small differences from the exact Beta answer are Monte Carlo error.

```{r predictions}
set.seed(1)
y_new <- rbinom(nrow(draws),50,draws$p)
y_plugin <- rbinom(nrow(draws),50,.4)
knitr::kable(tibble(method=c("posterior predictive","plug-in p = 0.4"),
                    q5=c(quantile(y_new,.05),quantile(y_plugin,.05)),
                    q95=c(quantile(y_new,.95),quantile(y_plugin,.95))))
tibble(survivors=c(y_new,y_plugin),
       method=rep(c("posterior predictive","plug-in"),each=nrow(draws))) |>
  ggplot(aes(survivors,fill=method)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth=1,position="identity",alpha=.5)
```

The predictive interval includes uncertainty about $p$ and random survival
given $p$. The optional changed-input comparisons in the first table use
exact Beta calculations; they are not default Stan draws relabelled as new fits.
